# DFIR «Расследование» — test datasets and their ground truth

Two log sets for exercising the incident-investigation pipeline (timeline →
findings → links → report). Load a set's folder in «Расследование» → «Построить
шкалу», with the year **2026** for syslog lines that carry no year. The lists
below are the ground truth to compare the engine's output against — what was
actually done, and what the engine is expected to find.

No Python is needed: the files are checked in ready to load.

---

## 1. `real-web-incident/` — a REAL capture

This is **not** hand-written. A real nginx was started in a container and real
HTTP requests were fired at it with `curl`; `web01/access.log` is the genuine
access log nginx wrote. The source address is `127.0.0.1` because the attack
ran on the same host (a lab), so it is an internal source.

- Chain of custody: `web01/access.log` SHA-256 =
  `2052bddec3b97ee50069dc8f0709218caed12ab1648e755cf5f5a9b703b58476`
  (the engine recomputes this; it must match).
- Benign traffic: 10× `GET /index.html` → 200.
- Recon: 20 distinct admin-panel probes → 404.
- Attack payloads (URL-encoded, one each): SQL injection (`' OR '1'='1`,
  `UNION SELECT`), path traversal (`../../../../etc/passwd`), SSTI (`{{7*7}}`),
  OS command injection (`;cat /etc/passwd`), PHP wrapper LFI (`php://filter`).

**Expected findings (7), all actor `127.0.0.1`:**

| severity | rule | MITRE | from |
|---|---|---|---|
| high | web-sqli | T1190 | the two SQL payloads |
| high | web-path-traversal | T1083 | `/etc/passwd` traversal |
| high | web-rfi-lfi | T1190 | `php://` wrapper |
| high | web-ssti | T1190 | `{{7*7}}` |
| high | web-cmd-injection | T1190 | `;cat /etc/passwd` |
| high | web-webshell | T1505.003 | *see note* |
| medium | web-path-scan | T1595 | the 20 distinct 404s |

**Expected links: none.** One host, one internal source — correct: cross-host
links are raised only for an external source spanning several hosts.

**Known loose match (honest note):** `web-webshell` fires here partly on the
`cmd=` parameter of the command-injection request and on `eval` inside the
`…/eval-stdin.php` recon probe. Those are a recon probe and a cmd-injection
attempt, not an actual web shell — the webshell signatures (`cmd=`, `/eval`)
are broad. A real incident would still want a human to confirm it; worth
tightening later.

---

## 2. `synthetic-incident/` — a full two-host scenario (hand-built)

Hand-built logs for the parts a single-host lab cannot safely stage (SSH
brute-force with a successful break-in, post-breach sudo commands, and
cross-host correlation from an **external** attacker). Laid out per host
(`web01/`, `db01/`) so host attribution and links work. Mixed with benign
internal traffic so false positives are visible. Generated by
`scripts/gen-incident-corpus.py` and checked in here so it loads without Python.

Scenario: attacker `45.137.21.134` brute-forces SSH on both hosts and breaks
the shared `deploy` account, then (as `deploy`, via sudo) installs netcat,
runs `curl http://… | bash`, and wipes journals; on `web01` the account
`svc-update` is created. Separately `185.220.101.47` scans `web01` for admin
panels and fires web-attack payloads. Benign: `ubuntu` logs in by key from
internal `10.0.3.11`/`192.168.1.50`; normal `GET /index.html` 200s.

**Expected findings (11):**

| severity | rule | actor |
|---|---|---|
| critical | ssh-bruteforce-success | 45.137.21.134 |
| critical | cmd-log-clearing | deploy |
| high | web-sqli / web-path-traversal / web-ssti / web-cmd-injection / web-webshell | 185.220.101.47 |
| high | cmd-download-exec | deploy |
| medium | web-path-scan | 185.220.101.47 |
| medium | account-created | svc-update |
| medium | cmd-offensive-tool | deploy |

**Expected links (2):**

| severity | rule | actor | hosts |
|---|---|---|---|
| high | link-ip-multi-host | 45.137.21.134 | db01, web01 |
| high | link-account-multi-host | deploy | db01, web01 |

The benign `ubuntu` / internal-IP activity must **not** produce a link (its
source is internal) — that is the false-positive suppression working.
